name: open-vsx
description: Open VSX Registry (open-vsx.org), the open-source VS Code extension marketplace. This CLI searches extensions and reads extension details, versions, README/CHANGELOG files, reviews, publisher namespaces and the registry change feed through its public JSON API.

commands.name: search-extensions
commands.summary: Search Open VSX extensions by keyword, with optional category filter, sorting and offset paging

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search term. Omit it to list all extensions, for example the most downloaded or most recently updated.

params.name: category
params.description: Category name filter, e.g. Linters, Themes, Programming Languages, Snippets, Debuggers, Formatters

params.name: offset
params.description: Number of results to skip, for paging

commands.name: get-extension
commands.summary: Get full metadata of the latest version of an extension: description, files, links, all version URLs and download count

params.name: namespace
params.description: Publisher namespace, i.e. the part before the dot in the extension id

params.name: extension
params.description: Extension name, i.e. the part after the dot in the extension id

commands.name: get-extension-version
commands.summary: Get metadata of one specific version of an extension. The version can also be 'latest' or 'pre-release'.

commands.name: get-extension-file
commands.summary: Fetch a text file from an extension version, such as README.md or CHANGELOG.md. The request redirects to the content CDN.

params.name: version
params.description: Exact version string. Use get-extension to find the latest one.

params.name: fileName
params.description: File name as listed in the extension's files map. It is case-sensitive, e.g. README.md, readme.md or CHANGELOG.md.

commands.source: E15 E16 E17 E18 E19 E20 E21 GET https://open-vsx.org/api/ms-python/python/2026.4.0/file/README.md

commands.name: list-extension-reviews
commands.summary: List user ratings and review comments for an extension

commands.name: list-extension-versions
commands.summary: List published versions of an extension, newest first, as a version-to-URL map with offset paging

params.name: size
params.description: Number of versions per page (server default 18)

commands.name: query-extensions
commands.summary: Query extension metadata by id (namespace.name), with optional version and all-versions flag; returns one entry per target platform (e.g. linux-x64, alpine-arm64, universal)

params.name: namespaceName
params.description: Return extensions of this namespace only

params.name: extensionName
params.description: Extension name, used together with namespaceName

params.name: includeAllVersions
params.description: Return one entry per version instead of only the latest

commands.name: get-namespace-details
commands.summary: Get a publisher namespace's profile (display name, description, website, social links) and its extensions with stats

commands.name: list-namespace-extensions
commands.summary: List the names of all extensions in a namespace (a map of name to API URL) and whether the namespace is verified

commands.name: list-version-changes
commands.summary: Page through the registry-wide feed of extension version changes (publish/state updates), oldest first, using a cursor

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque nextCursor value from the previous page

commands.name: get-registry-version
commands.summary: Get the Open VSX server version and limits, such as the maximum extension size

notes: Extension ids are 'namespace.name' (e.g. redhat.java). Path-based commands take them split into namespace and extension.

Version-specific file URLs (README, CHANGELOG, .vsix, icon) are listed in the 'files' object of get-extension / get-extension-version. File names are case-sensitive (redhat/java uses readme.md, ms-python/python uses README.md).
get-extension-file returns raw text and follows a 302 redirect to openvsx.eclipsecontent.org. Binary files such as .vsix should be downloaded from files.download instead of being read as text.
search-extensions uses offset paging: the step equals size (30 by default). totalSize gives the total number of matches.
The cursor parameter name for list-version-changes was inferred and not seen in the recording. Pass the nextCursor value from the previous response; hasMore=false marks the end.
All commands are anonymous reads. Publishing, reviewing and deleting need an Open VSX access token and are not covered. The full OpenAPI spec is at /v3/api-docs/registry.
